body: The Federal Aviation Administration temporarily paused departures nationwide on Friday, November 13, while flights already in the air were allowed to continue to their destinations. American said the five-hour ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, and the airline focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible that evening while positioning aircraft and crews for the recovery. For the rest of that evening, American said it prioritized flights to non-hub cities and international flying.

Recovery continued through the weekend. On Saturday morning, American said the previous day's ground stop had led to significant cancellations and delays, and that lingering effects would continue that day. By Saturday evening, the airline said all planned cancellations for that night and the following day had been completed, and its focus was on positioning crews and aircraft for a strong start. On Sunday afternoon, American reported improvement, with fewer cancellations as work to fully restore the operation continued.

In its latest update, on Sunday night, American said: "American is prepared to operate a largely normal schedule Monday, Nov. 16, following the FAA's nationwide ground stop." The airline said crews and aircraft were in position, favorable weather was expected across its system, and it did not anticipate additional broad cancellations related to the disruption. A travel alert remains in effect, allowing customers to change their plans or request a refund, and American advised passengers to check their flight status on its app or website before heading to the airport.
en.summary: American Airlines says it is prepared to operate a largely normal schedule on Monday, November 16, after the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday disrupted flights across the United States, with crews and aircraft in position and no additional broad cancellations expected from the event.
en.title: American Airlines says Monday flights largely back to normal after FAA nationwide ground stop

body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）11月13日週五暫停全美航班起飛，空中航班則可繼續飛往目的地。美國航空表示，這次全國停飛約五小時，週五晚間解除後，公司把重心放在當晚盡可能營運剩餘航班，同時調度飛機與機組為後續恢復做準備；當晚優先保障非樞紐城市與國際航班。
恢復作業延續整個週末。週六上午，美國航空表示，前一日的全國停飛造成大量取消與延誤，影響當天仍會持續；到了週六晚間，公司表示當晚與隔日的所有計畫性取消皆已完成，重心轉為讓機組與飛機就位、迎接隔日營運。週日中午過後，公司表示恢復已有進展，取消班次減少，正持續全面恢復營運。
週日晚間的最新通報中，美國航空表示已準備好在11月16日週一營運大致正常的航班表，機組與飛機皆已就位，全線天氣預期良好，預期不會再因這起事件出現大規模取消。旅遊警示仍然有效，旅客可更改行程或申請退票；美國航空提醒旅客前往機場前，先在官方應用程式或網站確認航班狀態。
zh.summary: 美國航空表示，聯邦航空總署11月13日全國停飛造成全美航班大亂後，公司已準備好在11月16日週一營運大致正常的航班表，機組與飛機皆已就位，預期不會再因這起事件出現大規模取消。
zh.title: 美國航空：FAA全國停飛後營運恢復、週一航班大致正常
